units: 1 stud = 1 Blender unit. Sizes and offsets are in studs; set each MeshPart's Size from 'size'.
axes: Roblox axes (Y up). Blender (x, y, z) -> Roblox (x, z, -y); an asset's front (Blender -Y) faces Roblox +Z. The asset origin is the bottom centre of its footprint: a piece's MeshPart sits at origin CFrame * CFrame.new(offset); VFX positions are relative to the same origin.

palette.uv: row i, level j: u = (j + 0.5) / columns, v = 1 - (i + 0.5) * cell / height (v up from the bottom of the image); a row's spare cells repeat its last level

water.uv: Water pieces carry their own UVs (not palette cells): a box projection in studs from the asset origin, one texture tile per tile_studs. Up-facing faces: u = X / tile, v = Z / tile (mod 1, Roblox axes); faces toward +-Z use (X, -Y), toward +-X use (-Z, -Y). Set MeshPart.TextureID to the uploaded texture (it wraps), Transparency from the piece, Material SmoothPlastic, CastShadow false. Assets placed on a tile_studs grid continue the pattern seamlessly.
water.flow: Pieces of an asset with a water_flow socket carry flow = {direction (unit, Roblox X/Z), speed (studs/s), socket}. To animate, use a Texture (Face Top, StudsPerTileU/V = tile_studs) on the piece instead of TextureID and move OffsetStudsU/V along direction * speed each frame.

assets.name: ShoreIslet
assets.subject: ShoreIslet
assets.notes: 32x32 shore islet: tall narrow columnar rock pinnacle (~12 x 9.5 base, rock top z~14, ~16 with the tiny grass cap) on a sand collar in an octagonal sea slab with 7 satellite boulders; precise so players can walk the sand, ledges and summit (the w03_water surface and skirt export as see-through non-colliding water; the seabed, the collar's under-water slope and the rock bases below z=1.0 are w03_riverbed). The reference's 'Foam Ring' part is NOT a mesh: it is the water_foam sockets VFX_ShoreIsletFoamRing_N (18: one every ~5 studs round the sand collar waterline at z 1.05 (scale 0.7), plus one round each of the 7 boulders standing in the water, scale 0.6-0.8 by size; emitter made denser and more opaque for a bold white surf line). VFX_ShoreIsletSpray_N: two faint vapour sea-spray hazes (0.6) at the windward front-left foot of the stack and the big front-left boulder. VFX_ShoreIsletFlow_N: one slow water_flow beam lying across the back water at z 1.03 (west -> east drift).
